prompt: Janitor or Trove for cleaning up connections in my Roblox UI code?
result:
Janitor. This project already uses it (see `CLAUDE.md`), so adding Trove would mean two cleanup libraries doing the same job.

They overlap heavily, so the project's choice matters more than any feature gap. Both give you `Add`, a cleanup call, and instance-bound cleanup. Janitor also lets you remove a single item (`Remove`, `Get`) and link cleanup to an Instance with `LinkToInstance`.

In the Vide UI code, Janitor isn't the right tool for everything. Vide ties cleanup to its own reactive scopes, so inside a component use `cleanup()` or an `effect`. That covers connections you make while a component renders. Keep Janitor for things that live outside a Vide scope, such as client controllers, services, and long-lived objects.

If you have a specific leak or a component you're unsure about, point me at it and I'll say which side it belongs on.
